security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU TCG translates and executes Zalasr load-acquire/store-release instructions (opcode 0x2f, funct3=0-3 for loads, funct3 encodes in upper bits for stores) without: (a) checking natural alignment before memory access and raising the appropriate misaligned exception (LoadAddressMisaligned/StoreAmoAddressMisaligned), or (b) inserting memory ordering barrier primitives (acquire after load, release before store) corresponding to the aq/rl bits encoded in the instruction. In multi-hart SMP emulation, the absence of these barriers means the TCG translator does not emit the necessary host memory fences, allowing cross-hart memory operation reordering that violates the acquire/release semantics the guest synchronization code depends on.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: translator decodes Zalasr opcode 0x2f with aq/rl bits set but does not call gen_load_acquire / gen_store_release barriers, or skips gen_alignment_check before gen_load/store
security_spec.summary: Zalasr instructions mandate natural alignment traps and acquire/release memory ordering; QEMU must enforce alignment in TCG before access and emit host memory fences when aq/rl bits are set, otherwise multi-hart guest synchronization code suffers silent data races
